summary: Iteration 1 achieved a perfect score of 100/100 on the tree permutation sorting problem. The algorithm combines all-pairs BFS routing, tree DP max-weight matching, and depth-parity alternating anti-oscillation. The control arm confirmed that without these components, the score drops to 5/100.
key_points: h-main scored 100/100 (predicted ≥90), confirming the tree DP matching + alternating anti-oscillation algorithm works optimally across all 20 test cases including random trees, path graphs, and bushy trees.

h-control-negative scored 5/100 (predicted ≤10), confirming that naive greedy without tree DP or anti-oscillation fails due to oscillation — the 95-point gap validates both algorithmic components as necessary.

The problem appears fully solved at score 100. A second iteration could investigate robustness (re-measure to confirm the 100 is stable vs. the earlier 95-99 variance seen during development), but there is no remaining performance gap to close.

Key principle discovered: type-1 swaps (one element benefits, one is displaced) cause period-2 oscillation on trees; gating them by depth-parity edge coloring alternating each round breaks the cycle while still allowing convergence in O(n) rounds.
Recommendation: APPROVE to continue only if robustness verification is desired; otherwise this campaign can be concluded at score 100/100 with high confidence.
